newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia PM threatens to quit in row with president.
newsitem.headline: Latvia PM threatens to quit in row with president.

text.p: Latvian Prime Minister Andris Shkele on Monday tendered his resignation amid a row with the Baltic state's president over the proposal of a candidate for finance minister who was under investigation by the prosector's office.

The surprise resignation bid came after President Guntis Ulmanis called on members of parliament not to back Vassily Melnik, who was proposed by Shkele and a leading government party as finance minister.
Shkele said in a statement "the president and the political elite accused me of pressing upon them amoral decisions".

"I do not see a possibility of continuing to lead the government without the trust of both the president and parliament following these irresponsible, totally groundless and too grave accusations," Shkele told a press conference.

The controversy over Melnik, a 29-year-old businessman, erupted after a newspaper alleged the proposed minister was being investigated for a conflict of interests by holding private and state posts at the same time.
The prosecutor's office confirmed Melnik was being investigated but later said he had not broken any laws. It was unknown if the investigation had concluded.
Shkele defended himself in his decision to back Melnik, saying he fully trusted the Democratic Party Saimnieks, the largest faction in parliament, that had proposed the candidate.
He said as far as he was concerned he had been honestly working for the good of the country.
"I have done all within my powers to secure the functioning of the government but I have to conclude that the task has proved to be too difficult," Shkele said. "My conscience is clean."
The president's office said Ulmanis was still considering Shkele's resignation. The two men are to meet after 1800 GMT on Monday to discuss the situation.
Shkele is seen as one of the main forces behind Latvia's attempts to speed up the reform process launched after it quit the former Soviet Union in 1991.
A non-party businessman, he was asked by Ulmanis to take office at the end of 1995 after two previous attempts to find a prime minister in Latvia's fractured parliament failed.
Shkele has led an eight-party coalition government and managed to pass key legislation despite frequent internal bickering.
One of Shkele's main achievements has been to pass the country's first-ever balanced budget for 1997.
He has also been a key force behind the acceleration of the Baltic state's privatisation process.
Latvia's efforts to attract more foreign investment were given a boost last week when international credit rating agency Standard & Poor's gave the country an investment grate rating.
